Subject: Partner adaptor compatibility — request for timeline and guardrails

Hi Sofia,

Hope you’re well — quick ask from our engineering and product teams. We’re planning to adopt Redwood SDK v4 but have a number of customers and integrations that still rely on v3 adapter code. Before we commit to a migration schedule internally, we need clarity on Redwood’s official coexistence policy for major SDK bumps:

- How long will you support v3 after v4 GA?
- Are there recommended adapter patterns or official shims that Redwood will ship?
- Any required compatibility tests or certs we should run?

Our timeline is aggressive; we’d like to start work next sprint but need to align on a minimum compatibility window so we can coordinate our roadmap and customer comms. Attaching a brief compatibility questionnaire and a snapshot of our integration matrix.

Attachment: compat-request.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks — can you loop in whoever owns partner SDK policy?

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for the attachments. I’ve pulled in folks who own policy and Dedicated/SLA considerations. Below is a proposal we can iterate on; we’ll also follow up with a quick sync to align timelines.

Proposed Redwood partner coexistence policy (initial draft):
- Support window: 9 months of full backward compatibility for official SDKs after v4 GA. After the 9-month window, we provide a 3-month security-only patch period for critical fixes.
- Tiered windows: For Dedicated/Reserved accounts with contractual SLAs, extend the full compatibility window to 12 months if requested at time of GA (requires a written request and ops gating).
- Official shim/adaptor: Redwood will publish an official minimal adaptor library (redwood-adaptor-compat) that implements the most common runtime shims (legacy auth headers, old batching semantics, and token schema translation). This library will be maintained during the full support window.
- Compatibility matrix & tests: We will publish an automated compatibility test suite (pytest + sample fixtures) that partners can run; passing tests will be a recommended precondition for certifying integrations before v3 sunset.
- Migration guidance: Detailed migration guide with canonical code snippets, common gotchas, and performance notes. We’ll also provide a recommended canary rollout plan for partners to minimize production risk.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal review: Marcus — can you confirm the Dedicated extension and whether 12 months is OK operationally?
2) Vanesa/Platform — can you validate that we can commit to maintaining the adaptor library for the 9/12 month window and outline the release cadence?
3) Schedule a 30-minute call next week with Catalyst engineering to walk the compatibility matrix and canary plan.

I’ve attached an initial draft of the coexistence policy and a compatibility matrix template for us to fill in during the sync.

Attachments: proposed-coexistence-policy.md (text/markdown, 8 KB), compatibility-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 24 KB)

Thanks — happy to iterate.

—Sofia

Sofia / team,

Putting a quick operational note here: for Dedicated customers (and for partners that run on reserved pools for customers), I want us to default to the 12-month compatibility window rather than 9 months. The reasoning: switching infra or re-qualifying on-prem customers often requires longer lead times and procurement cycles. If we expose two windows without guidance we’ll end up managing multiple exception requests.

Suggested language tweak:
- Default: 12 months full compatibility for all integrations that are in active production at GA.
- Expedited sunset (9 months) can be offered for non-production/test-only adapters where the partner requests a faster cadence (e.g., if they want to adopt v4 earlier).

Operational asks:
- Product/Platform to confirm the adaptor maintenance SLA (monthly patch window + emergency fixes).
- Legal to confirm if we need to add a contractual notice period for Dedicated customers (I can loop legal if this moves forward).

Happy to discuss on the call — this is a sensible place to lock in expectations.

—Marcus
